idiom_name: EF Core keyset query (Where/Take) with a cursor DTO
implementation_notes: The classic Cursor/Page/Codec structure collapses into one LINQ query plus a small token DTO: EF Core documents keyset pagination as the recommended alternative to Skip/Take, so you keep the ordering-key values of the last row (base64url-encoded) and issue OrderBy/ThenBy plus Where(p => p.Date > last.Date || (p.Date == last.Date && p.PostId > last.Id)).Take(pageSize).ToListAsync(); IAsyncEnumerable<T> with await foreach streams the pages without buffering them all. Factor the composite predicate into one extension method per endpoint family; the classic hand-rolled form is only justified when the query engine cannot express the predicate (EF Core cannot translate row-value comparisons like (Date, Id) > (@a, @b) in LINQ).
pitfalls: An ordering that is not fully unique (date without the id tiebreaker) silently skips or duplicates rows across pages - EF Core's docs warn that relational databases apply no default ordering, so the composite predicate is mandatory.
EF Core cannot translate row-value comparisons such as WHERE (Date, Id) > (@a, @b); the expanded OR form changes the execution plan, so verify the index still covers both sort columns.
